Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
28-year-old woman with new-onset unilateral throbbing headache since yesterday; no focal or systemic red-flag features.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Left posterior headache, onset yesterday mid-morning, gradually intense, 8/10 throbbing pain.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies nausea, vomiting, visual disturbance, photophobia, focal neurological deficits, fever, chills, rash; pain not positional or diurnal.  
• Pertinent negatives: No prior similar headaches.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Medications: None regular. Took Nurofen (Ibuprofen) yesterday; no relief.  
• Allergies: None reported.  
• Family history: Mother with hypertension and migraines.  
• Social: Lives with partner; designer; non-smoker; no alcohol or recreational drugs.

Examination:
• No vitals or physical examination performed (teleconsult).

Impression:
New-onset unilateral throbbing headache—likely primary headache disorder (migraine vs tension); no current red-flag features.

Plan:
• Prescribed stronger NSAID (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) to be taken regularly with food; may combine with Paracetamol.  
• Supportive measures: Rest, adequate hydration.  
• Safety-net advice: Seek urgent review if headache worsens, persists beyond 1–2 days despite treatment, or if fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, or recurrent episodes develop.  
• Follow-up: Contact clinic in 1–2 days if no improvement.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected elements: Vitals, neurological examination, formal medication/allergy reconciliation, specific drug name/dose.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor repetition, no significant inaudible segments.
